title: Sebastian and the Prom
premise: Beatrix Oyelaran transfers to Ashgrove Academy, a school built over the sealed ruins of a Victorian theater, where a century-old bargain demands a 'championship' of performances to keep the thing below asleep. When drama teacher Ms. Voss pairs Beatrix with her nemesis Sebastian Wren for the semester showcase, they discover the school's beloved prom tradition is actually the ritual's cover — and this year, the seal is failing. To survive, they must win the meaningless student talent championship to earn the right to perform at the prom, then win the real contest against the theater's original star, a ghost who has never lost her final audition. Beatrix chooses to break the cycle of inheritance rather than claim the power it offers, freeing the ghost and the school at the cost of the showcase she came to Ashgrove to win.
about_author: Mirabel Delacroix is a former stage manager who spent six years working in converted theaters across the American Midwest before turning to writing full-time. She lives in an old opera house apartment with her cat, Ophelia, and insists the building's cold spots are just drafty windows.

chapters.title: The New Kid Is Fine
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Arriving at Ashgrove Academy mid-semester, Beatrix navigates hostile hallways, a guidance counselor who flinches at the word 'theater,' and the school's obsessive prom culture. She hears faint music from beneath the gym floor. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness masked by aggressive cheerfulness — she's fine, obviously.

chapters.title: Assigned Partners
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Ms. Voss pairs Beatrix with Sebastian Wren, the school's golden boy and Beatrix's instant rival, for a semester project on the school's founding. Researching in the archive, they find a 1924 program for a theater that officially never existed. Emotional beat: friction sparking into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Foundation Is Made Of
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Following the program's clues, Beatrix and Sebastian find a bricked-up stairwell behind the auditorium and descend into the sealed Odeon theater, perfectly preserved. A voice asks them to 'hold the note.' They flee. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian confesses his family has 'held' the school for generations — his grandmother performed the prom ritual in 1968. The championship that doesn't matter (the talent show) selects who gets to perform at prom, the championship that does. Emotional beat: the weight of inheritance, and Sebastian's resentment of it.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Two
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Forced to prepare a talent-show act together, they train in the Odeon after hours, where the ghost — Adela Marsh, the theater's lost star — coaches Beatrix in exchange for small favors. Beatrix's voice strengthens unnervingly fast. Emotional beat: growing trust shadowed by a bargain neither fully understands.

chapters.title: Preliminaries and Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They win the talent-show preliminary, but Beatrix discovers Sebastian knew the ritual's cost — the winner's voice is 'kept' by the house afterward, as Adela's was. Feeling used, she walks out. Emotional beat: betrayal, and Sebastian's guilt over a lie of omission.

chapters.title: The Seal Cracks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With no winner chosen, the Odeon begins leaking — cold spots, chorus voices in the vents, students sleepwalking toward the auditorium. Ms. Voss, herself a former 'winner,' reveals the seal fails at the next prom unless someone performs the final audition. Emotional beat: shared fear forcing reconciliation.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Reunited, they perform their act at the talent championship and win — deliberately, together, on their own terms. That night Adela reveals the truth: the final audition isn't a ritual, it's a competition, and she has never lost, because losing means ending. Emotional beat: triumph undercut by the real stakes.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At prom, above the packed gymnasium, Beatrix and Sebastian audition against Adela in the Odeon — not to defeat her, but to out-sing her grief. Beatrix offers Adela the inheritance instead: someone to remember her, so she can stop performing. Adela falters, and lets go. Emotional beat: climax — compassion as victory.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The seal dissolves peacefully; the Odeon becomes a warm, ordinary space. Sebastian's family burden lifts, and Beatrix, who lost her chance at the showcase, performs anyway at an unofficial after-prom in the old theater — for no one, for everyone. Emotional beat: found family, chosen endings, and a home finally hers.
